'''Donald Cameron McIntosh''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRSE}} (13 January 1868 – 1 July 1957) was a Scottish educator and mathematician.

== Biography ==
McIntosh was born at [[Kirkmichael, Banffshire|Tomintoul, Banffshire]], Scotland on 13 January 1868. He was educated at Tomintoul Parish School and [[Aberdeen Grammar School]]. He studied at the [[University of Aberdeen]] graduating with a MA in 1890, a BSc in [[Marine biology|marine zoology]] 1906 and a DSc in 1912 with a thesis entitled ''Studies on Echinodermata and on Variation''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Former Fellows of The Royal Society of Edinburgh 1783 – 2002 (part 2)|publisher=Royal Society of Edinburgh|year=2006|isbn=0-902198-84-X|location=Edinburgh|pages=586}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/McIntosh.html|title=Donald McIntosh (1868 - 1957)|website=[[mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk]]|access-date=2019-12-29}}</ref>

From 1890 to 1899 he was a teacher at George Watson's College, in Edinburgh, and Head of Mathematics at [[The Mary Erskine School|Edinburgh Ladies' College]] from 1899 to 1918. From 1918 to 1933 he was Director of Education in Moray and Nairn.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

He was a member of the [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]] and the [[Royal Physical Society of Edinburgh]].<ref name=":0" />

He was elected as a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 1903. His proposers were [[John Sturgeon Mackay]], [[Francis Grant Ogilvie|Sir Francis Grant Ogilvie]], Sir John Murray and [[Alexander Morgan (mathematician)|Alexander Morgan]].<ref name=":0" />
